citation.title: Deep learning-based topological optimization for representing a user-specified design area

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the best 80% of predicted designs, mean compliance differs from the SIMP solutions by 2.75% on average.
claim.location: conclusion, first quantitative classical comparison; section 4.3.2 and Table 2
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 4.3/Table 1: 0.4393 s SIMP divided by 0.07634 s CNN per case = 5.7545; paper also calls this an 83% time reduction.
claim.alternatives: Conclusion also reports 99.6% design-area satisfaction and an 83% time reduction versus SIMP; section 4.3/Table 1 gives paired times. Abstract qualitatively claims lower computation time.

baseline.implementation: MATLAB open-source 88-line topology optimization code of Andreassen et al. (section 4.2)
baseline.hardware_classical: same CPU as CNN; CPU model not stated (section 4.3)
baseline.hardware_ml: same CPU as SIMP; CPU model not stated (section 4.3)
baseline.data_generation_cost: 370,000 SIMP-generated designs; generation time not stated (section 4.2)
baseline.quality_metric: Mean compliance error, volume fraction error, and design-area satisfaction (section 4.3.2; Table 2)
baseline.quality_gap: Top 80%: 2.75% mean compliance error; lower 20%: 103872% average error; mean volume fraction error 9.70%; 99.6% meet design-area threshold 0.01 (section 4.3.2; Table 2)

R1.evidence: Conclusion: first quantitative comparison with SIMP is 2.75% compliance error for the best 80% of predictions; speed is a later alternative.

R2.evidence: Conclusion: selected primary outcome compares design quality, while Table 1 gives a separate speed claim.

R3.evidence: Conclusion: selected primary outcome compares design quality, while Table 1 gives a separate speed claim.

R4.evidence: Section 4.3.2/Table 2: [inferred] compliance of returned density fields is evaluated by FE, and volume/design-area errors are reported. Disconnected examples and extreme errors in the lower 20% are discussed, but their failure rate is not counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: 37,000 test designs (section 4.2); 296,000 training and 37,000 validation designs

notes: The first quantitative classical comparison in the conclusion is a quality result, so the primary stratum is quality despite the later 83% speed claim. The reported 2.75% compliance error excludes the worst 20%; Table 2 reports 103872% average error for that lower-ranked fifth. Section 4.3 says both times used the same CPU but gives no processor model or warm-up protocol.
